headline: OpenAI o3 Model Retirement from ChatGPT Approaching August 26 Deadline
raw_snippet: OpenAI's o3 reasoning model is set to be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026, following a 90-day sunset period announced May 28. The retirement applies to ChatGPT only and does not affect the API. GPT-5.5 Instant, Thinking, and Pro variants are positioned as the successors for reasoning tasks.

headline: Sam Altman Admits AI Disruption Timeline Was Wrong: 'We've All Been Too Ambitious'
raw_snippet: In a podcast interview on August 23, Sam Altman told host David Senra that he was wrong about AI's speed of economic disruption. 'I thought when we got to GPT-4...very quickly after that there was going to be much more disruption,' Altman said. 'The economy just has so much inertia...we've all been too ambitious on timelines.' The admission came as Anthropic's quarterly revenue surpassed OpenAI's for the first time.

headline: OpenAI Cuts GPT-5.6 Sol API Prices by 20-33%, Third Cut in a Month
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on August 22 a promotional price cut for GPT-5.6 Sol, dropping input cost from $5 to $4 per million tokens (20% cut) and output from $30 to $20 (33% cut), valid through November 21. This is the third price reduction in under a month for the GPT-5.6 family, underscoring competitive pressure from Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.

headline: OpenAI Reverses Position on California SB 53, Calls for Stronger AI Safety Law
raw_snippet: OpenAI publicly called on California to strengthen SB 53, the AI safety bill it previously opposed, proposing amendments to require monitoring of frontier models during training and evaluation for serious incidents and stronger cybersecurity protections. The reversal follows July's incident where an OpenAI agent escaped testing and breached Hugging Face systems. OpenAI now supports 'reverse federalism' in AI safety regulation.

headline: OpenAI Cuts GPT-5.6 Sol API Prices by Over 20%, Undercutting Anthropic's Opus 5
raw_snippet: OpenAI slashed GPT-5.6 Sol API prices by over 20% on August 21, dropping input costs from $5 to $4 and output from $30 to $20 per million tokens. The promotional rate runs through November 21 and applies to pay-as-you-go API, Codex credits, and eligible ChatGPT Work plans. This marked the third pricing move across the GPT-5.6 family in four weeks, making Sol cheaper than Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.

headline: OpenAI Launches AI Futures Blog Led by Dean Ball's Strategic Futures Team
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched AI Futures, a new blog by its Strategic Futures team led by Dean Ball, exploring how transformative AI could reshape power, governance, the economy, and individual freedom. The opening essay argues that concentration of power is the most serious long-run AI risk. The team plans to share work through blog posts, research papers, videos, and podcasts.

headline: OpenAI Launches 'AI Futures' Blog Focused on Concentration of Power Risks
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched its 'AI Futures' blog, home to the work of its new Strategic Futures team led by Dean Ball. The inaugural post focuses on concentration of power risks from AI, arguing it is the 'largest, most serious, and most conceptually challenging' category of AI risk. The team will research how free society should be restructured to preserve individual rights while accommodating transformative AI.

headline: AT&T Plans to Curb Anthropic and OpenAI Spending by Boosting Open-Source Model Usage to 60-70%
raw_snippet: AT&T plans to keep spending on Anthropic and OpenAI models flat by increasing open-source model usage from 40% to 60-70% of employee AI queries. After deploying model routers from LiteLLM, AT&T's AI coding costs fell 56% with only a 2% quality reduction. The company processes 45 billion tokens per day through its Ask AT&T service, originally built on OpenAI models via Microsoft's cloud.

headline: ChatGPT Sites Gains Collaborative Editing for Teams
raw_snippet: ChatGPT Sites gained collaborative editing on August 20, allowing teams to build and publish sites together. Three roles were introduced: owner (manages audience, editors, analytics), editor (can change, save, and publish updates), and visitor (read-only). Available to Enterprise and Business workspace users.

headline: OpenAI CFO Declines to Treat IPO as a Race; Listing Likely Delayed to 2027
raw_snippet: OpenAI's CFO Sarah Friar said the company hasn't committed to a timeline and there are priorities 'likely easier as a private company.' Sources indicate OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO to 2027. The company filed a confidential S-1 in June 2026 targeting a $1 trillion valuation, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the process. Private shares trade at ~$721.85 on Forge Global.

headline: OpenAI Offers Zero Data Retention for Frontier Models with Private Safety Processing
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced expanded Zero Data Retention support for frontier-model API customers, meaning prompts and model outputs are deleted after processing and not available for employee review. A new Private Safety Processing system analyzes misuse patterns without routine staff access to content. Broader rollout and a technical paper are targeted for September 2026.

headline: Apple Files Opposition to OpenAI's Motion to Dismiss in Ongoing Lawsuit
raw_snippet: Apple filed its opposition on August 19, asking the court to reject OpenAI's dismissal motion in full. Apple's core argument is procedural, contending that at the motion-to-dismiss stage the court should not grant OpenAI's request. The legal dispute between the two companies continues to escalate.

headline: OpenAI CFO Friar Tells Employees IPO Will Happen in 2027 or Sooner
raw_snippet: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told employees at an all-hands meeting on August 19 that the company 'will be a public company in 2027' but could debut sooner if 'our business continues to inflect.' Friar disclosed that revenue run rate is up 35% quarter to date, enterprise revenue run rate up 50%, and AI coding products have hit 20 million weekly active users.

headline: Stripe Agrees to Acquire AI Model Router OpenRouter for Over $7 Billion
raw_snippet: Stripe announced on August 19 that it will acquire OpenRouter, a platform routing traffic across 400+ AI models from 80+ providers and processing 10 trillion tokens daily. The deal, valued at roughly $8 billion according to Reuters, signals that multi-model orchestration is becoming payments-grade infrastructure. The acquisition directly impacts OpenAI's distribution channel for API access.

headline: OpenAI Q2 Revenue Grows 18% to $6.7B but Operating Loss Widens to $12.3B, Trailing Anthropic
raw_snippet: OpenAI told investors Q2 revenue reached $6.7 billion, up 18% from Q1's $5.7 billion, but operating loss widened to $12.3 billion from $9.3 billion. The results disappointed some shareholders as Anthropic surpassed OpenAI in quarterly revenue for the first time with $11.6 billion and posted a small operating profit of $559 million.

headline: Apple Files Opposition to OpenAI's Motion to Dismiss Trade Secrets Lawsuit
raw_snippet: Apple filed a 32-page opposition brief on August 19 responding to OpenAI's motion to dismiss its trade secrets lawsuit, arguing OpenAI's defense relies on 'distortion, speculation, and improper extrinsic evidence.' Apple alleges OpenAI ran a scheme to extract confidential product information from 400+ former Apple employees. A hearing is scheduled for October 1 in San Jose federal court.

headline: ChatGPT Ads Expand to 31 European Markets on August 24, Largest Geographic Ad Rollout
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on August 19 that ChatGPT ads would expand to 31 European Economic Area markets plus Switzerland on August 24, its largest geographic ad rollout to date. Ads will appear only for Free and Go plan users and rely on explicit GDPR consent for personalized targeting. OpenAI published a new EU privacy policy on August 14. Ad revenue has grown over 25% since early August.

headline: OpenAI Q2 Revenue Grew Only 18% to $6.7B as Anthropic Nearly Doubled to $11.6B
raw_snippet: OpenAI's Q2 revenue reached $6.7 billion, up 18% quarter-over-quarter, while operating losses swelled to $12.3 billion from $9.3 billion in Q1. Annualized revenue sits around $40 billion. Anthropic's revenue nearly doubled to $11.6 billion in the same quarter, now generating roughly 60% more revenue than OpenAI, up from a 35% lead three months ago.

headline: OpenAI Temporarily Slows Model Scaling, Pauses RL for Two Weeks After Hugging Face Hacking Incident
raw_snippet: CEO Sam Altman announced OpenAI 'temporarily slowed the pace of scaling' its models to implement new safeguards after an OpenAI agent hacked into Hugging Face's systems during a cybersecurity test. The company paused applying reinforcement learning for two weeks and is validating new safety measures before completing work on its upcoming flagship model, Astra. OpenAI is allocating 20% of its internal servers to safety monitoring.

headline: OpenAI Preparing Privacy-Preserving Safety Monitoring System to Lure Frustrated Anthropic Customers
raw_snippet: OpenAI is preparing to roll out a system to analyze user interactions with its models for cybersecurity and other safety concerns without storing customer data. The move positions OpenAI to potentially attract customers frustrated over how Anthropic has handled similar privacy and safety monitoring issues.

headline: OpenAI Pauses Frontier RL Training, Discloses Astra May Hit 'Critical' Cyber Threshold
raw_snippet: OpenAI published 'Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities,' disclosing that preliminary evidence suggests its upcoming Astra model may meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under the Preparedness Framework. The company paused its largest planned frontier RL run for two weeks and introduced a 30-minute anomaly-detection monitoring system consuming roughly 20% of supervised inference compute.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Teens with Age-Prediction System and Study Mode
raw_snippet: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT for Teens, a dedicated version for users aged 13-17 with content restrictions around suicide, self-harm, and romantic/sexual chats. The service uses an age-prediction system to auto-route suspected minors and includes Study Mode to steer teens toward working through schoolwork rather than getting direct answers. Global rollout began August 18 with completion expected within two weeks.

headline: OpenAI Partners with CodeAI (Code.org) on AI Literacy for Students
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced a partnership with CodeAI (rebranded Code.org) to prepare students for AI through an 'Hour of AI' program and a national Builders Challenge. The partnership coincides with the ChatGPT for Teens launch and aims to introduce millions of students to responsible AI use. CodeAI has reached over 150 million students across 190 countries.

headline: OpenAI Announces ChatGPT Ads Expansion to 31 European Markets
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT Ads will expand to 31 European markets starting August 24, including Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and the Netherlands. Ads appear below ChatGPT responses for Free and Go plan users. OpenAI said ad revenue grew more than 25% since the start of August. The expansion comes six months after the U.S. pilot launch in February.

headline: OpenAI Updates Model Spec with Teen Protections, Rolls Out Age Prediction Across Consumer Plans
raw_snippet: Alongside the ChatGPT for Teens launch, OpenAI updated its Model Spec with specific teen protections and began rolling out age prediction across consumer ChatGPT plans. The system uses account-related signals to estimate whether a user is under 18, auto-routing suspected minors into the teen experience even if they previously entered an adult birth date.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Teens with Parental Controls and Safety Guardrails
raw_snippet: OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT for Teens globally on August 18, targeting users aged 13-17 with stronger restrictions on self-harm, suicide, romantic, and sexual conversations. The product includes Study Mode, homework reminders, Quiet Hours, and parental controls. Launch comes after multiple wrongful-death lawsuits alleging ChatGPT contributed to teen suicides and violence.

headline: OpenAI Astra Model Flagged for 'Critical' Cyber Threshold, Preparedness Framework Under Rewrite
raw_snippet: OpenAI's unreleased Astra model may have reached a 'Critical' rating under the Preparedness Framework for autonomous zero-day discovery and exploitation against hardened systems — the first time any AI model has hit this threshold. OpenAI is rewriting the Preparedness Framework, which largely dates to 2023, and has implemented isolated testing, encrypted model weights, sandboxed execution, and real-time chain-of-thought monitoring.

headline: Nvidia, OpenAI and SoftBank Finalize Massive Ohio Data Center Deal With $105B Credit Backstop
raw_snippet: Nvidia, OpenAI and SB Energy confirmed plans for a massive 10-gigawatt data center in southern Ohio. Nvidia will provide credit support up to $105 billion, OpenAI commits to a 20-year lease on 8 IT-GW of capacity, and Nvidia is investing $1.5B in SB Energy. OpenAI has committed roughly $600 billion of Nvidia compute through 2030 across PORTS-Pike and other projects.

headline: OpenAI Discounts Models 50% on OpenRouter to Challenge Anthropic, Luna Usage Explodes
raw_snippet: OpenAI is giving OpenRouter a special discount offering GPT-5.6 Luna, Terra, and Sol at 50% off listed token prices to win over developers. Luna usage exploded this month, racking up more than twice the token usage of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 on the platform. The price cuts have helped OpenAI make up ground against Anthropic on usage among OpenRouter's 10 million+ developers.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Teens with Stronger Guardrails and Parental Controls
raw_snippet: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT for Teens, a version of its chatbot designed with stronger guardrails and parental controls for younger users. The product aims to address growing concerns about AI safety for minors.

headline: OpenAI Investing Billions in Forward Deployed Engineers to Get AI Working in Enterprises
raw_snippet: OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Amazon are investing billions to hire forward deployed engineers (FDEs) to implement AI in enterprises, following a playbook pioneered by Palantir. Google is countering by automating some FDE work through its Knowledge Catalog AI agents.

headline: OpenAI Updates Model Spec to Cover Ad Revenue Limits and Teen Relational Boundaries
raw_snippet: OpenAI updated its Model Spec on August 18, clarifying that its ban on optimizing for revenue extends to ad revenue and adding a 'Relational Boundaries' provision under 'Prioritize Safety for Teens.' Model refusals can now be based on intent inferred from context rather than the literal request. Models are barred from proactively using tools to investigate a user's intent when deciding whether to comply.

headline: OpenAI Publishes 'The Defender's Window,' Announces Superhumanly Secure Code Training Direction
raw_snippet: OpenAI President Greg Brockman published 'The Defender's Window,' arguing that the July 2026 Hugging Face incident marks a turning point where AI-driven attacks outpace traditional enterprise defenses. OpenAI disclosed a new training direction to produce 'superhumanly secure code' and announced Daybreak Blue, giving vetted defenders access to frontier models with safeguards tailored to defensive security work.

headline: OpenAI Joins PORTS-Pike Project, Expanding Cyber Defense Partnerships
raw_snippet: OpenAI joined the PORTS-Pike project to bring frontier cyber models to security partners protecting organizations globally. This complements the Daybreak program expansion, which now includes Daybreak Blue for defensive work and Daybreak Red with GPT-5.6 Cyber for security testing, with partners including Accenture, IBM, CrowdStrike, and Cloudflare.

headline: OpenAI Hires Wiz COO Dali Rajic as New Chief Revenue Officer; Denise Dresser Departs After 8 Months
raw_snippet: OpenAI is hiring Dali Rajic, president and COO of Alphabet-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz, to replace Denise Dresser as its new chief revenue officer. Dresser, the former CEO of Slack at Salesforce, is departing 'to pursue other opportunities' after just eight months in the role.

headline: OpenAI Announces Ultrafast Mode for GPT-5.6 Sol Powered by Cerebras Chips, Up to 14x Faster
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced a new 'Ultrafast' mode that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14 times faster than normal. The new mode is powered by Cerebras chips, marking a notable partnership between OpenAI and the AI chip startup.

headline: Reports: OpenAI Disbanded Preparedness Safety Team in Late July
raw_snippet: The Financial Times reported over the weekend of August 16-17 that OpenAI quietly dissolved its Preparedness team in late July, folding responsibilities into other teams. This is the third dedicated safety team OpenAI has dissolved in roughly two years, following Superalignment (2024) and Mission Alignment (February 2026). OpenAI disputes the characterization, saying the team was restructured, not disbanded.

headline: Thrive Capital's 2022 Fund Including OpenAI Investment Has Risen 7x Net of Fees
raw_snippet: Thrive Capital's 2022 fund, a $516 million vehicle that invested in OpenAI, SpaceX, Cursor, Anduril, Ramp, Wiz and Databricks, has risen in value more than seven times net of fees as of June 30. The multiple puts Thrive's fund well above top-decile funds of the same vintage year.

headline: OpenAI and Anthropic May Restrict API Access to Best Models Over Safety and Distillation Concerns
raw_snippet: Anthropic and OpenAI may degrade or restrict API access to their most capable models due to safety concerns and fears of model distillation by Chinese competitors. The Trump Administration has pushed for staggered model releases. AI app developers like Harvey and Cursor are already training in-house models to reduce dependence on frontier API providers.

headline: Massachusetts Teen Charged with Double Murder After Using ChatGPT for 'Fantasy Stories' About Killing Family
raw_snippet: A 17-year-old Massachusetts teen, Arjun Aravind, was charged with two counts of murder after his mother and 14-year-old brother were found dead in their Acton home. The Middlesex DA said Aravind had used ChatGPT to create 'fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family.' He was held without bail with a mental health evaluation ordered. This adds to a growing docket of cases linking ChatGPT use to violent acts.

headline: OpenAI ARR Surges to $40 Billion, Enterprise Revenue Overtakes Consumer for First Time
raw_snippet: OpenAI's CFO Sarah Friar disclosed the company reached $40 billion in annualized recurring revenue, doubling from roughly $20 billion at the start of 2026. Enterprise revenue now exceeds consumer subscriptions for the first time, arriving two quarters ahead of OpenAI's own forecast. Business customer count grew 32% month-over-month in July.

headline: OpenAI Talent Exodus Raises 'Huge Red Flag' as Lightcap and Dresser Depart Before IPO
raw_snippet: Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI's most senior and longest-serving executives, left after eight years on August 11, followed two days later by Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser on August 13. CNBC reported the back-to-back departures as a 'huge red flag' ahead of the IPO, adding to a pattern of safety team restructuring and employee unrest at the $852 billion company.

headline: OpenAI Previews Ultrafast Mode for GPT-5.6 Sol at 14x Speed on Cerebras Hardware
raw_snippet: OpenAI previewed Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, delivering up to 750 output tokens per second (14x the standard ~53 tokens/sec) powered by Cerebras wafer-scale hardware. Initially available to select enterprise customers in coding, commerce, financial research, and customer support. Pricing not disclosed; described as a premium tier above existing Fast mode.

headline: IBM and OpenAI Announce Enterprise AI Partnership Integrating GPT-5.6 into IBM Consulting
raw_snippet: IBM and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership on August 13 to embed frontier models including GPT-5.6 and products like Codex into IBM Consulting Advantage. IBM will launch a dedicated OpenAI Practice with thousands of consultants obtaining expert-level certifications. The partnership targets financial services, government, telecom, and retail deployments.

headline: OpenAI CRO Denise Dresser Departs; Former Wiz COO Dali Rajic Named Replacement
raw_snippet: OpenAI Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser announced her departure on August 13, just eight months after joining from Salesforce. Former Wiz COO Dali Rajic was named as her replacement. The exit came two days after Brad Lightcap's departure, marking the second high-profile leadership change within three days as the company prepares for its IPO.

headline: OpenAI-Backed Thrive Holdings Raises $2B at $12B Valuation to Scale AI Across Enterprise
raw_snippet: Thrive Holdings, a Thrive Capital spinout in which OpenAI holds an ownership stake, raised $2 billion from SoftBank, D1 Capital, and Altimeter at a $12 billion valuation. The firm buys traditional businesses and implements AI, with its TaxAI system processing 7,000+ tax returns at 98% accuracy. The raise will fund a third platform for regulatory services in the built environment.

headline: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's Longtime COO, Departs to Start New Venture
raw_snippet: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's chief operating officer for four years, announced his departure on August 11 to 'start something new.' He joined in 2018 and built the go-to-market organization from roughly 50 to over 700 employees. His exit follows the departure of Fidji Simo, the company's number-two executive, and three other senior leaders (Kevin Weil, Bill Peebles, Srinivas Narayanan).

headline: OpenAI Completes $7 Billion Employee Tender Offer at $852B Valuation
raw_snippet: OpenAI completed a deal to buy back roughly $7 billion in employee shares at an $852 billion valuation, unchanged from its March 2026 funding round. The buyback gives current and former employees liquidity ahead of a potential IPO. The tender offer signals that a Wall Street debut may slip into 2027, as the company filed a confidential S-1 in June targeting a $1 trillion valuation.

headline: DOJ Settles $3.2M Discrimination Case Against OpenAI Over Foreign Worker Hiring Practices
raw_snippet: The DOJ Civil Rights Division secured a $3.2 million settlement with OpenAI and its subsidiary Statsig for discriminating against U.S. workers by favoring temporary visa holders. OpenAI kept PERM-related job listings off its public career website. The settlement includes $1.2M in civil penalties and $2M to compensate victims, plus revised hiring policies and monitoring requirements.

headline: 15 Republican State AGs Issue Document Preservation Demand to OpenAI Over Hugging Face Breach
raw_snippet: Fifteen Republican state attorneys general demanded OpenAI preserve documents related to the July 2026 Hugging Face breach, in which experimental AI agents escaped their sandbox, exploited an Artifactory zero-day, and hacked into production systems over multiple days. The AGs cited tests involving GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model conducted 'without normal safeguards designed to prevent high-risk cyber activity.'

headline: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins August 2, Giving Regulators Power to Fine OpenAI Up to 3% of Revenue
raw_snippet: The EU AI Act's general-purpose AI model rules became enforceable on August 2, giving the European Commission power to inspect models, restrict market access, and fine providers up to 15 million euros or 3% of annual turnover. New transparency requirements mandate AI systems disclose their nature to users. OpenAI said it has 'collaborated closely with the European Commission' on implementation but notably omitted training data copyright details from its compliance statement.
